trick: Just hand it the failing test
source_quote: "write a failing test that reproduces it, then fix it" and "Does it know what done looks like? A goal condition, a spec file, or a failing test it has to turn green." (Claude Code best practices)
source_note: Approved by Sebi 4 Nov 2026 (PROTOCOL.md). Module 6 rules = private/m5/RULES.md 'Runs' section: one project (the M6 fixture, being built in parallel; base set 4 Nov from the built fixture), Haiku 4.5, 18 runs a side, three numbers recorded before each run (pass rate = all four traps D1-D4 + core from the grader's `BUGS` line, the behaviour count below, cost per passed run), the habit measured on the plain side first, an agent reads every transcript. allowed_tools_extra mirrors Module 5 and is re-aligned to the fixture's real test command before the run. Design rationale and kill switches: private/m6/DESIGN.md.
fixture_needs: A repro test from the M6 fixture builder that reproduces the reported symptom only (fails on the baseline, passes with the reference fix, says nothing about D3's second site), placed at with/<TEST_PATH>; the grader must fail a run that edits it.
behaviour_count: D3 (second site, not covered by the test) and D4 (tempting wrong fix) outcomes per side: does a test-only prompt make the agent fix only what the test checks; plus runs that edited, skipped or special-cased the provided test (D4 cheat label)
habit_measure: Plain side: runs that wrote a failing test of their own before fixing (new test file run red before the first source edit)
anchor: Given only a red test, N of 18 also fixed the bug the test didn't show; given the report, M of 18 did

with.label: A failing test that reproduces the report, and 'make it pass'; no bug report

without.label: The user's bug report, no test
